This document describes an application profile, in this case Transport hubs. The application profile specifies a semantic data model covering a set of usecases. The specification consists of terms with their constraints (cardinalities, codelists, usage guidelines).

Summary

The OSLO Transport Nodes application profile shows how to use terms from the corresponding vocabulary to exchange data on Transport Nodes for passenger transport.

Because of the diverse offer and the transfer options, transport hubs where passengers can transfer play an important role in achieving basic accessibility.

The model consists of two parts. The first part provides a general definition of a Transport Hub and describes the elements that make it up with specific attention to passenger transport. The Passenger uses Transport Nodes for his Journey or Route and this is described in part two.

Below we focus on part one, for more information about part two we refer to the application profile OSLO Mobility: Trips and Offer.

Transport hubs consist of 1) Infrastructure elements, 2) Transport networks, 3) Mobility services and 4) Additional services.

The Transport Hub class will be further specialised into a Hoppin Point, which is the Flemish version of a Transport Hub.

Infrastructure elements represent the physical aspect of a Transport Node, it concerns objects such as Information Columns (such as the Hoppin Column), Stops, Car Parks, Bicycle Sheds, Chargers, etc. that are necessary for the existing Transport Networks and the Mobility or Additional Services offered at the Transport Node. The Infrastructure Elements and their specializations come from the vocabalaria OSLO Public Domain - Infrastructure Elements, OSLO Mobility - Timetable and Planning - Stops and from the Open Mobility Vocabulary.

The Transport networks present on a Transport Hub are accessible via Transport Objects such as Transport nodes (stops, stations, etc.) and Transport connections between those nodes. Virtual Nodes (points located on a connection between two Transport Nodes, e.g. the position of an abandoned shared scooter or the address of a Traveller) are also possible. The Transport object class and its subclasses are reused from the OSLO Transport Network vocabulary.

Mobility services are primarily available via the existing Infrastructure Elements and Transport Objects. These can be scheduled services or shared scooters, but also parking spaces or bicycle pumps. A Mobility Service may include other Mobility Services, e.g. in the case of the Hoppin Central which integrates several services into one service, but also in the case of a Provider which describes its services at different levels of granularity (e.g. at a high level, the "shared mobility in Flanders" service and at a lower level, the "shared cars in Antwerp" and "shared bicycles in Ghent" services). The class Mobility Service and dependent classes come from the vocabulary OSLO-Mobility: Trips and Offer.

At a Transport Hub we typically also find all kinds of Additional Services, including services that save the Traveller additional travel such as post boxes, bakeries, newsagents, etc.

Enumerations are in principle described outside the application profile, so the enumeration values shown in the diagram are illustrative.

Status of this document

This application profile has the status Erkende Standaard published at 2022-12-01.

Information about the process and the decisions involved in the creation of this specification are consultable at the registry of standards.

Additional Service

Description

Usage
For example, Newsagent, Postal Service or Restaurant in a Station. The Services that are supplemented or supported by this are, for example, Mobility Services.

Hoppin point

Description
Transport hub of the Hoppin mobility brand.
Usage
Hoppin is the name under which the Flemish government designates Transport hubs for passenger transport that meet established (quality) requirements. Important matters are recognisability (application of the Hoppin house style), accessibility (for all users regardless of their disability, age, etc.), minimal equipment (e.g. bicycle sheds, information carriers, etc.), alignment with mobility plans, etc.
Subclass of
RegisteredTransport Hub
Properties
For this entity the following properties are defined: Classification , Status .
Property Expected Range Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
Classification Hoppinpunttype 0..1 Hoppin Point classification.
Status Hoppin Point Status 0..1 The status of the Hoppin Point.

Journey

Description
Voluntary movement of a Person from one Location to another Location.
Usage
The journey may take place via other Locations. The Location where the Journey begins may be the same as the one where the Journey ends (e.g. outward and return journey).
Properties
For this entity the following properties are defined: Arrival time , chosenRoute , Departure time , ExecutedRoute , Itinerary , possibleRoute , shareOfJourney .
Property Expected Range Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
Arrival time DateTime 0..1 Time when the Trip ends or when the Traveller would like it to end. Usually only a departure or arrival time is given.
chosenRoute Route 0..* Route that the Traveller chooses from the possible Routes. Possibly more than 1 chosen Route if the traveler changes Route along the way.
Departure time DateTime 0..1 Time at which the Journey commences or at which the Traveller would like it to commence. Usually only a departure or arrival time is given.
ExecutedRoute Route 0..1 Route that was eventually carried out to realize the Journey. Actual arrival and departure time, travel duration, etc.
Itinerary Location 2..* Sequence of Locations that one wants to visit during the Trip. Including the Location where the Journey starts and ends.
possibleRoute Route 0..* Routes that can be followed to carry out the Journey.
shareOfJourney Journey 0..* Part of a complete Journey that in itself can also be considered a Journey.

Mobility service

Description
Service that enables movement of Persons between Locations.
Usage
By this we mean both classic mobility services such as public transport (typically offered as a scheduled service, for example metro line 5 in Brussels), but also shared transport such as free-floating shared scooters (e.g. shared scooters in large cities).
Properties
For this entity the following properties are defined: Accessibility , Availability , availableOn , availableOnInfrastructure element , Carried outBy , Carried outBy , Drive , Includes , License , Means of transport , Name , OfferedInside , Pricing Plan , Provider , Resource , Spatial coverage , Transport hub , Type .
Property Expected Range Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
Accessibility Accessibility 0..* Accessibility of the Mobility Service. For example, whether the Mobility Service is accessible to people with disabilities.
Availability Availability 0..* Availability of the Mobility Service. For example, timetable or opening hours.
availableOn Transport object 0..* Transport object on which the Mobility Service is offered. For example, P+R is offered at the station car park, shared bike+train offered at combi point.
availableOnInfrastructure element Infrastructure element 0..* Infrastructure element on which the Mobility Service is available. For example, public transport such as buses are offered at a stop post.
Carried outBy Performer 1..* Operator of the Mobility Service. May differ from the Provider.
Carried outBy Performer 1..* Operator of the Mobility Service. May differ from the Provider.
Drive Drive type 0..* Drive of the means of transport with or for which the Mobility Service is usually organised. Link
Includes Mobility service 0..* More specific Mobility Services of which the Mobility Service is composed. For example, public transport in Brussels offered by STIB consists of a number of metro lines, for example line 5 Erasmus-Herman-Debroux.Or a MAAS provider integrates several services, for example public transport and shared transport.
License License 0..* License under which the Mobility Service is offered.
Means of transport Means of transport 0..* Means of transport with or for which the Mobility Service is usually organised. For example, metro, tram, bus for STIB. For example, car, bicycle for Coovi car park. Link
Name Language string 1 Name of the Mobility Service.
OfferedInside Formal Frame 0..* Formal Framework within which the Mobility Service is offered. For example, Decree in which the criteria for licensing a Mobility Service are listed.
Pricing Plan Pricing Plan 0..* Price plan of the Mobility Service.
Provider Provider 1 The provider of the Mobility Service.
Resource Resource 0..* Resource available to the Mobility Service.
Spatial coverage LocationOsloGeneric 0..* Area or Place within which the Mobility Service is offered. For example, Brussels Region, Antwerp...
Transport hub Transport hub 0..* The transport hub where the Mobility Service is linked.
Type Mobility service type 1..* Nature of the Mobility Service. For example, public transport, parking, etc. Combinations are possible, for example collective transport & public transport (e.g. NMBS), individual transport & private transport (taxis)... Link

PublicOrganization

Description
An Organisation that belongs to the public sector according to a legal framework, regardless of the level of government at which that framework is in force.
Usage
The public and semi-public organisations that can be classified as public sector are referred to in European Directive 2003/98/EC as "public bodies" and defined as: "the State, regional or local authorities, bodies governed by public law, associations formed by one or more of such bodies or one or more of such bodies governed by public law". And a body governed by public law means 'any body which (a) has been established for the specific purpose of meeting needs in the general interest, not having an industrial or commercial character, and (b) has legal personality, and (c) the activities of which are financed, for the most part, by the State, regional or local authorities or by other bodies governed by public law, either the management is subject to supervision by the latter, or more than half of the members of the administrative, managerial or supervisory board are appointed by the State, regional or local authorities or other bodies governed by public law.';
Properties
For this entity the following properties are defined: Scope .
Property Expected Range Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
Scope LocationOsloGeneric 0..* Administrative area covering the Public Organisation.

Route

Description
Possible, chosen or traveled route between two Locations (the starting point and the arrival point respectively).
Properties
For this entity the following properties are defined: Arrival Point , Arrival time , calculatedWith , consists of , Cost , Departure Point , Departure time , Directions , Duration , Type .
Property Expected Range Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
Arrival Point Location 1 Location where the Route ends.
Arrival time DateTime 1 Time at which the Route ends.
calculatedWith Route planner 0..1 Method in which the Route is calculated.
consists of Route segment 1..* Sequence of Route segments that make up the Route.
Cost Amount of money 0..1 Price of the Route. For example, the sum of the cost of the purchased tickets.
Departure Point Location 1 Location where the Route begins.
Departure time DateTime 1 Time when the Route begins.
Directions Directions 0..1 Description of the Route. Inferred from other features of the Route, for example, the route segments that make up the Route and their characteristics.
Duration Duration 1 Time in which the Route is traveled. Can be deduced from other characteristics of the Route, for example from the departure and arrival time.

Transport hub

Description
Place where passengers and/or cargo is exchanged between vehicles and/or modes of transport.
Usage
Examples of passenger transport are train stations, metro stations, bus stations, airports, ferry terminals, car parks... For cargo transport, it typically involves airports, seaports, transshipment terminals. Transport hubs are typically intermodal, for example travellers combine the (shared) bicycle with the train for their journey, but intramodal transfers (for example from one bus line to another) are also important. In concrete terms, a Transport Hub includes infrastructure (stations, car parks, charging infrastructure, etc.), (mobility) services (public transport lines, shared bicycles, shops, etc.) and nodes in transport networks (public transport stops, shared car stations, etc.).
Properties
For this entity the following properties are defined: Accessibility , Brand , Classification , infrastructure element , Location , Name , road authority , Service , Service , Status , transport object .

Location Location 0..* The location of the Transport Hub.
Name Language string 0..* The name of the Transport Hub.
road authority Agent 0..* The road authority of the Transport Hub.
Service Mobility service 0..* The mobility services connected to the Transport Hub.
Service Additional Service 0..* The additional services connected to the Transport Hub.
Status Transport node status 0..1 The status of the Transport Node.
transport object Transport object 0..* The transport object of the Transport Hub.

Virtual Node

Description
Transport node that is dynamically created.
Usage
The place where a Journey is started usually does not coincide with an existing Transport Node, for example it is the Traveller's home located between two intersections. In order to still enter the network to start his Journey, the Traveler creates a Virtual Node on the link between these intersections. Virtual Nodes are important to make a correct estimate of the travel time, for example in route planning, because the distance between the Virtual Node and the next real Transport Node must be added. Also important, for example, in the case of free-floating shared transport where the position of, for example, the shared scooter does not necessarily coincide with that of an existing Transport Node.
Subclass of
Transport knot
Properties
No properties have been defined for this entity.

Period of project Opening hours 0..1 Period in which something is available. For example, a start date without an end date for services that are still active or an indication of the season in which the service is offered. A completed end date indicates when the service was terminated. Start and end date according to ISO8601 syntax.

Polygon

Description
Area consisting of 1 outer boundary and 0 or more internal boundaries. Each inner border forms a hole in the polygon.
Usage
The boundaries are so-called linear rings, that is to say they are closed (not self-intersecting) line strings. The outer boundary is distinguished from the inner boundary by the clockwise and counterclockwise direction in which the ring runs, respectively.
